column1: # jar-r1.tsv -- DUMPBIOS, the cookie jar: one case per cookie tag, and the jar
# as a whole (number of entries, tags in order), against EmuTOS 1a7484ab
#   jar:<TAG>  the value of the first entry with that tag, zero-extended, or
#              "absent".  EXACT = present or absent on both sides with the
#              same value; PTR_RAM / NONZERO = present on each side and the
#              property holds; ABSENT = absent on each side
#   jar:*      the number of entries before the terminator and their tags,
# A jar case issues no trap: the dumper reads _p_cookies ($5A0) and the jar
# through the backend's td_jar_read -- Supexec on the m68k
# (tosdump/abi/m68k_scrninfo.c), a plain load of the per-process page 0 on
# NewTOS (tosdump/abi/newtos_scrninfo.c) -- what any program reads there.
# The jar's capacity (the terminator's value) is not measured.
# The rows: every tag EmuTOS names (include/cookie.h:26-44, the ones
# fill_cookie_jar adds in its order first), then the two NewTOS adds
# One table for the oracle's profiles tt, falcontc and disk
# (tools/hatari-oracle.sh): a class that is not EXACT holds on all three
# (tosdiff --selfcheck).  The machine cookies differ between the profiles
# and are EXACT.  A difference against NewTOS: docs/COMPATIBILITY.md, the
# cookie jar entry (ADR-012 and its amendments, docs/MEMORY.md).
# One table, frozen once measured: a case id is the physical line number
# and the dump header carries the CRC of this file.
